content: LLMs are probabilistic pattern-matchers, not calculators: they produce plausible-looking arithmetic from memorized patterns (e.g. 200x197 errors), and even with tools available they often fail to invoke them unprompted (dev.to Jun 2025; HN Feb 2025). Clinical-calculator research (arXiv 2026) argues a single numerical error changes outcomes, requiring deterministic solvers wrapping LLMs. Consensus fix: enforce routing of ALL math to deterministic code (Python/executed functions), never rely on model-generated numbers; force tool use in workflow design rather than hoping the model chooses it.
